title: Will Smith in Talks for Indian Film Debut as Villain in Atlee's Rs 800 Crore Sci-Fi Epic With Allu Arjun
excerpt: The Oscar-winning actor, who has long expressed his desire to work in Bollywood, is reportedly negotiating to play the main antagonist in one of the most ambitious Indian films ever mounted.
body:
• Will Smith is reportedly in talks to play the main antagonist in director Atlee's upcoming sci-fi action film with Allu Arjun, currently titled AA22xA6
  • The Rs 800 crore film, produced by Sun Pictures, would mark Smith's first major role in an Indian production
  • Smith previously revealed failed collaboration attempts with Salman Khan and Amitabh Bachchan, and publicly urged Shah Rukh Khan to cast him in a Bollywood project
  • The film's cast already includes Deepika Padukone and Mrunal Thakur, with Hollywood-grade VFX planned by studios behind the Avengers franchise

Will Smith's long-stated ambition to work in Indian cinema may finally be taking shape. The Oscar-winning actor is reportedly in advanced talks to play the main antagonist in director Atlee's highly anticipated sci-fi action film alongside Allu Arjun, according to multiple industry reports from Cinema Express, Bollywood Hungama, and other outlets.

From Red Carpets to Real Talks

Smith's interest in Bollywood has been an open secret for years. At the January 2026 Dubai premiere of his National Geographic series Pole to Pole, the Bad Boys star revealed that earlier collaboration attempts with two of Bollywood's biggest names had fallen through.

https://x.com/MissMalini/status/2090486831217516905

"I was talking to Salman. We had things we were talking about. I was trying to get into something with Big B, you know. He told me I could be Big W, so we were cool — we were sharing the title. There were a couple of things over the years… nothing panned out."

— Will Smith, speaking to Gulf News

Smith also made a direct pitch to Shah Rukh Khan, looking straight at the camera and saying, "I want Shah Rukh to put me in something. Shah Rukh, what's up?" The moment quickly went viral on social media.

The Atlee-Allu Arjun Mega-Project

The vehicle for Smith's potential Indian debut is AA22xA6, a working title for the massive sci-fi action thriller being helmed by Atlee, the director behind Shah Rukh Khan's blockbuster Jawan, which grossed over Rs 1,100 crore worldwide. Allu Arjun, riding the global success of Pushpa 2: The Rule, headlines the project.

Produced by Sun Pictures on a reported budget of Rs 800 crore, the film is based on a reincarnation storyline blending science fiction with commercial Indian cinema. Allu Arjun is expected to take on dual roles, potentially setting up a direct on-screen face-off with Smith in high-octane action sequences.

The project's ambitions extend beyond casting. Atlee and Allu Arjun have already visited leading VFX studios in Los Angeles, including facilities that worked on the Avengers and Transformers franchises. "We are bringing in all the latest technologies. My focus is on creating a visionary cinematic experience," Atlee said at a recent event.

A Star-Studded Ensemble

Deepika Padukone has been confirmed for a prominent role, with Mrunal Thakur and Janhvi Kapoor also reportedly in consideration. If Smith signs on, the film would feature one of the most internationally diverse casts in Indian cinema history.

Reports suggest that if negotiations with Smith don't materialize, the makers have a backup plan: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson is also reportedly being considered for the villain's role.

A Shift in the Cross-Border Dynamic

Smith is not entirely new to Indian screens — he made a brief cameo in Karan Johar's Student of the Year 2 in 2019. But a full-fledged role as the primary antagonist would represent a significant milestone, reversing a trend that has largely seen Indian actors like Priyanka Chopra, Deepika Padukone, and the late Irrfan Khan cross over into Hollywood rather than the other way around.

"Many Indian actors are now enjoying significant opportunities in Hollywood, but Western actors rarely get equivalent chances in Bollywood. I want to change that dynamic."

— Will Smith

The project's timeline remains fluid. While early reports targeted a late 2026 release, the scale of post-production work may push it to early 2027. Neither Smith's representatives nor Sun Pictures have issued official confirmation of the casting.

If even a fraction of the reported ambitions come to fruition, the Allu Arjun-Atlee film could mark a turning point for Indian cinema's global reach — with Will Smith helping lead the charge from the other side.
